problem:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $15$ | $-13$ | $-5$ | $-4$ | $10$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying the Design Matrix When the Regression Curve Contains Zero Coefficients
examples.problem:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $6$ | $3$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y = \beta_0 + \beta_2 x^2 + \beta_3 x^3$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072333/assets/fe5d2bbb69e110d08d3231d486af483dc05d995e30907a5f9a62cf46743e81d7.png)

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector. Find $X$ and $\mathbf{y}$ in this context.
examples.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$\color{blue}1$** | **$\color{blue}2$** | **$\color{blue}3$** | **$\color{blue}4$** | **$\color{blue}5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $\color{red}6$ | $\color{red}3$ | $\color{red}2$ | $\color{red}4$ | $\color{red}6$ |

The coefficients of the curve

$$
y = \beta_0 + \beta_2 x^2 + \beta_3 x^3
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & {1}^{2} & {1}^{3} \\ 1 & {2}^{2} & {2}^{3} \\ 1 & {3}^{2} & {3}^{3} \\ 1 & {4}^{2} & {4}^{3} \\ 1 & {5}^{2} & {5}^{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3 \\ 2 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?
feedback.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $3$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $-1$ |

The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}^{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & {1}^{2} & {1}^{3} \\ 1 & 2 & {2}^{2} & {2}^{3} \\ 1 & 3 & {3}^{2} & {3}^{3} \\ 1 & 4 & {4}^{2} & {4}^{3} \\ 1 & 5 & {5}^{2} & {5}^{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.
